citation: Gunnerud UJ, Heinzle C, Holst JJ, et al. Effects of Pre-Meal Drinks with Protein and Amino Acids on Glycemic and Metabolic Responses at a Subsequent Composite Meal. PLoS ONE. 2012;7(9):e44731.
protocol: Standardised composite ham sandwich meal (white wheat bread 106.4 g, ham 27.7 g, etc.; ~50 g available carbohydrate; Table 1) with either 250 mL water or a pre-meal protein drink of 9 g whey or soy protein, with or without 5-6 added amino acids, taken with the meal within 12 min. Glucose and insulin at 0, 15, 30, 45, 60, 90, 120, 180 min.
population: 14 healthy non-smoking volunteers (5 men, 9 women), aged 20-28, normal BMI (~21.9); Sweden (Lund).

reports.where: Table 3: insulinaemic index, incremental peak; Table 4: early iAUCs per meal

note: The only protein-preload design kept (whey versus soy, in small doses), on a reference meal reported to the gram. Several results are in percent or index form relative to the reference meal, so absolute values need the reference row. Only in figures: insulin time course; GLP-1/GIP time courses (summary only in correlation table). Meal kinds: preload, mixed meal.
